# Practitioner Academy Proposal

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Program:** Practitioner Academy, AI Governance Academy
**Format:** 2 days, live virtual, four 90-minute working sessions per day
**Price:** US$12,500

## 1. Situation Summary

Dana Whitfield, the Profile Block lists Tamarack Instruments as a designer and manufacturer of laboratory measurement instruments, headquartered in the Netherlands and operating in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The block records three AI use cases:

* A customer service chatbot on the support portal (deployed).
* AI visual inspection on the German production line (piloting).
* AI sales forecasting (planned for next year).

AI maturity is recorded as Piloting. The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 is a certification target, with work to start next year and a start date not yet fixed. An internal audit finding of June 2026 records no inventory of AI systems.

Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The stated constraints are:

* Budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
* Customer data must stay in the EU.
* The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

## 2. Why Practitioner Capability Fits Now

The program responds to three recorded facts:

* **The audit finding.** It names a missing inventory, and the inventory is the first instrument the program builds.
* **The Q2 2027 objective.** It sets a horizon for governing the visual inspection pilot before production.
* **The ISO/IEC 42001 target.** It points toward an AI management system. The program builds working artifacts that later management system work could draw on. It does not promise certification or any audit outcome.

The proposed audience matches the recorded AUDIENCE_ROLES: General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors.

The program teaches three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

Participants work directly in two repositories:

* GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
* Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Two further references are used:

* AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards), the board-layer reference.
* The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done), the acceptance-layer reference.

## 3. Worked Examples and Their Selection

The program uses two running examples across both days.

1. **AI visual inspection (piloting).** It is selected because the stated objective names it directly. It also brings the works council constraint into the exercises and allows practice in EU AI Act classification reasoning.
2. **Customer service chatbot (deployed).** It is selected because it is the one use case recorded as deployed. It also brings the GDPR driver and the EU customer data constraint into the exercises.

AI sales forecasting enters the inventory exercise as a planned system. It is not a running example.

All exercises use sanitized analogs, so no customer data, production staff data or production imagery enters the sessions:

* Synthetic support transcripts describing invented instrument faults.
* An invented defect taxonomy and inspection decision log.
* An invented sales series.

## 4. Curriculum Spine

The facilitation kit for the fable is at https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md.

| Session | Exercise | Asset used | Artifact produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1, S1 | *The Turtle and the Phoenix*, told from the kit; handle map links the story to the workbook modules; twenty-minute closing exercise | Facilitation kit: story, handle map, section 8 closing exercise | The three artifacts specified in section 8 of the kit |
| Day 1, S2 | Draft accountability lines for the two running examples, with each role entered as `Unknown` until the Client confirms it | GRC Workbook module: governance structures | Draft governance structure |
| Day 1, S3 | Enter the chatbot, visual inspection and sales forecasting into an inventory; draft EU AI Act classification reasoning with open questions recorded | GRC Workbook module: AI system inventories and classification | Started AI system inventory |
| Day 1, S4 | Risk and impact assessment of visual inspection (works council precondition recorded) and the chatbot (EU data residency and GDPR recorded) | GRC Workbook modules: risk and impact assessments; policies and operating procedures | Draft risk register entries; draft operating procedure outline |
| Day 2, S1 | Write governed prompts for chatbot responses on synthetic transcripts | Slow AI Kitchen pattern: governed prompting | Governed prompt set |
| Day 2, S2 | Design the chatbot support workflow and the visual inspection review workflow on sanitized analogs | Slow AI Kitchen pattern: practical AI workflow design | Two governed workflows |
| Day 2, S3 | Place human checkpoints in both workflows and define acceptance criteria | Slow AI Kitchen pattern: human oversight and accountability; The Definition of Done | Oversight points and acceptance criteria per workflow |
| Day 2, S4 | Map the evidence each workflow generates; frame a board-level summary | Slow AI Kitchen pattern: evidence collection and audit readiness; AI Governance for Boards | Evidence map; draft board summary outline |

## 5. Deliverables

Participants leave with the following started artifacts, each stored in its repository location:

* A started AI system inventory covering the three recorded use cases.
* Draft risk register entries for visual inspection and the chatbot.
* At least two governed workflows: chatbot support and visual inspection review.
* The three section 8 artifacts from the fable session.
* A governed prompt set.
* Oversight points and acceptance criteria for each workflow.
* An evidence map.
* A draft board summary outline.

Ownership for finishing each artifact is `Unknown` and will be assigned at the close of Day 2.
